pages.lesson:
LESSON: VOLUME AND CAPACITY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.3 Area (8 lessons) • square metre (m2 ), acres, and hectares as u
Topic 3.4: Volume and Capacity

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Volume and Capacity. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Where do we use volume and capacity in daily activities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify metre cube (m3 ) as a unit of volume in measurements

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Volume and Capacity.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Volume and Capacity using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Make a cube of sides 1 metre using locally available materials
2. Discuss and work out the conversions of cm cube (cm3 ) to m cube (m3 ) and vice versa
3. Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner creates a conversion table of units of volume.
4. Creativity and Imagination: as the learner creates models of cubes and cuboids. Values
5. Responsibility: as the learner works with peers and share different tasks in making models.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Where do we use volume and capacity in daily activities?
2. Why do we measure volume?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Volume and Capacity is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
